claim: Down E6M5's flight (s304, s305, s314) Blood carries the side walls' courses on from step to step instead of restarting the tile on every tread (x_panning 8, 32, 56 at x_repeat 3), under one flat roof; E3M8 s113-s115 also keeps one flat roof over its steps, and E4M5 s113-s114 slope their ceilings with the flight rather than stepping them.
evidence: E6M5 s304, s305, s314: wall x_panning 8, 32, 56 at x_repeat 3, each the last plus x_repeat*8, ceiling 19,456 over all three (knowledge/blood/findings/probes/consolidation_audit3_p5.py)
E4M5 s113-s114: the ceilings slope (heinum -1,024) with the flight rather than stepping; E3M8 s113-s115 keeps one flat roof (ceiling 19,456) over its steps (checked 2026-11-26)
use: Lay every tread's side wall from one origin: x_panning continues by x_panning + x_repeat*8 in the wall's own direction, and y_panning moves with the roof by dz * y_repeat / 2048 texels (times 256 / tile height). For an existing run of step sectors call align_flights.

checked.how: Ran probes/consolidation_audit3_p5.py and read the sectors: E6M5 s304, s305, s314 side walls tile 67, x_repeat 3, x_panning 8, 32, 56 (each +24 = 3*8), y_panning 96 under one flat ceiling 19456. E4M5 s113, s114 ceiling heinum -1024. E3M8 s113-115 ceiling 19456 flat. But E3M1 s79's side walls are tile 20 at x_panning 0 and its tread s39 wears 67: no course carried on; E3M7 s88's neighbour s89 is at the same floor. Those two citations do not show it.
